lines: A smokehouse tells you fast who understands patience.
Empty hooks before supper can <shake>frighten</shake> a village more than thunder.
Salt is patient. That's why it keeps food better than most people keep promises.
Empty hooks tell a village to start worrying before anyone says it aloud.
People think about courage until supper is late. Then they think about supper.
A village with good stores can make careful choices instead of desperate ones.
Most days, I am at the smoker, trying to keep clean cuts from becoming everyone else's problem.
People think meat is simple until something goes wrong and suddenly it is very important.
A village runs on small work. Nobody praises it until it stops happening.
I trust a good cleaver more than a loud promise. The cleaver has less to prove.
When you had me follow you, I kept thinking the whole walk needed a sharper plan.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
Following you taught me that plans sound much safer before anyone starts walking.
I kept up, mostly. My feet have a harsher opinion of the trip.
Next time, warn me before the road becomes a test of character.
I learned two things out there: stay close, and ask better questions earlier.
You move like danger is a normal part of the route. I am still adjusting to that.
It was not all bad. Some views are worth sore legs and nervous glances.
If I followed you again, I would pack more food and fewer assumptions.
A boat ride is better than being dragged over rough ground. Still, I prefer cutting across town, not water.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It can't make me forget it.

Sharp knives are not angry knives. That's the first lesson.
A village eats better when nobody mistakes haste for skill.
I know every sound a clean cut should make. I also know when the street sounds wrong.

If you want my honest answer, slow down first. Rushed questions usually hide worse ones.
The village looks calm from a distance. Up close, it is mostly chores arguing with weather.
I notice the little things. That is either a skill or what the smoker has done to me.
